alerts.title: Renal and bone toxicity risk on TDF with hypertension and NSAID use
alerts.message: Guidelines advise TDF be avoided if eGFR < 50 mL/min/1.73m2 and that high-risk patients, particularly those with hypertension or diabetes, need closer renal monitoring at 3 and 6 months then 6-12 monthly. Patient has uncontrolled hypertension (146/94), trace proteinuria, and occasional ibuprofen use, all of which compound TDF nephrotoxicity risk. Creatinine 112 umol/L is within normal limits today, but the excerpts do not provide a fixed numeric eGFR threshold to confirm the current value against. Serum phosphate 0.78 mmol/L is low and is consistent with TDF-associated proximal tubular dysfunction, though this lab alone does not establish attribution. Persistent low back pain with thigh heaviness and stiff gait, in a patient on TDF, warrants evaluation for TDF-related bone mineral loss as well.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate eGFR today and repeat creatinine and eGFR per monitoring schedule; evaluate hypophosphataemia and proteinuria for tenofovir-related tubulopathy; stop ibuprofen; consider TDF alternatives (TAF) if renal or bone toxicity confirmed.

alerts.title: Suboptimal blood pressure control and amlodipine nonadherence
alerts.message: Guideline excerpts note hypertension as a risk factor for TDF-related renal harm and the plan addresses it with amlodipine refill and adherence counselling. BP today is 146/94 mmHg with admitted missed doses during transit, so adherence support is needed. Amlodipine adverse effects such as lower limb oedema are described in the excerpts, and none are present today (no pedal oedema).

evidence.recommended_action: Address amlodipine adherence barriers during travel, recheck BP at follow-up, and manage hypertension per guideline to reduce renal risk.
